## Samsung and SK Group Seal $950B in Aggregate Deals Covering HBM, Foundry, and AI Factory Supply as South Korea Hosts US AI Partners

A $950B aggregate commitment is a structural capex signal confirming the AI infrastructure build cycle is multi-year and deeply contracted; bullish for NVDA and AVGO supply security and for Korean semiconductor names as demand anchors, but also raises counterparty concentration risk if any relationship deteriorates.

- Samsung Electronics and SK Group announced combined deals totaling $950B with US AI technology companies.
- Coverage indicates deals span HBM memory, foundry capacity, and AI factory supply — multiple supply chain dimensions.
- NVDA and AVGO are among the counterparties per classifier tagging; Reuters confirms the headline aggregate figure.
- South Korea is positioning itself as a cornerstone of the global AI infrastructure supply chain.
